summary: Volume management and logistics keep finding gas allocated at a meter with no Sitara deal behind it: the deal has expired, covers the wrong days, or the volume is parked on Strangers Gas. They then email Daren Farmer, the deal owner, one request at a time to extend or create a ticket, and that request often waits a day or more. The fix is a daily exception job that compares allocated flow by meter and day with active Sitara deal terms and sends the owner a pre-filled extend/create/write-off request. Most of these items would then be caught the day after flow starts instead of months later, which removes the chasing emails worth about $184 a month ($2,208 a year).

current_workflow.step: A volume analyst or logistics scheduler sees flow or an allocation at a meter that no valid deal covers. The deal might have ended (286824 ends on 6/17), cover only some days (155118 is valid on 1/26 only), or not exist at all. Sometimes the item shows up in the allocation exception screen or as a Feedback Monitor error.
While waiting for a deal number, the analyst parks the volume on Strangers Gas, or in Volume Management with 'no detail', so the meter clears temporarily.

The analyst types up an email to the deal owner with the meter, deal number, dates and decatherms, and asks for an extension or a new ticket (e.g. extend 422516 for 10/6/2000, extend 465322 for 11/21/2000).
current_workflow.who: volume management analyst (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou)

current_workflow.step: If the owner is unclear or the request lands on the wrong desk, it gets forwarded between desks (the East desk to Daren, Julie to Daren, George/Craig asked to work out who should roll the deal).
current_workflow.who: traders / deal owners on HPL and East desks

current_workflow.step: Old or large items go to an approver, who asks why the gas was only found now before agreeing to a deal, a buy back or a write-off.

The deal owner extends or creates the Sitara ticket. Someone inserts the path in Unify, and the analyst re-allocates, gets track ids and closes the item. Volumes are often changed several times before it is closed.

stall_points.quote: It looks as though this meter is flowing starting 3/1/2000.

stall_points.description: The same meter comes back because the deal covers only part of the month's flow days, so a second request is needed.

stall_points.quote: I am uncomfortable putting a deal out there without more details.

stall_points.description: A very old request may not be processable at all because the period predates the current scheduling system.

solution.approach: A nightly job pulls allocated or measured volumes by meter and gas day from the volume and allocation data behind Volume Management and the allocation exception screen. It joins them to active Sitara deal tickets on meter and date. Each meter-day with flow is put into one bucket: covered; no deal; deal expired or outside its term (flow on days the deal does not cover); or parked on Strangers Gas. Next to each meter it shows the nearest existing deal number so the owner can see at a glance whether an extension will do. Exceptions are grouped per deal owner (the trader on the nearest deal, or a desk default when there is none) into one daily digest, rather than one email per meter. Each line carries the meter, the date range, the volume, the suggested deal to extend and three actions: extend, create new, or route to write-off/approval. Items stay open, with their age shown, until a covering Sitara deal appears or someone records a decision. Anything open past a set age, or tied to a payment deadline, is escalated to the desk lead.
solution.trigger: Nightly schedule after the day's allocations post, plus an on-demand run during month-end close
inputs: allocated and measured volumes by meter and gas day (allocation / Volume Management data)
active and recently expired Sitara deal tickets: deal number, meter, start/end dates, counterparty, trader
volumes currently placed on the Strangers Gas contract
Unify path records for the meter and date, to show whether a path exists
a maintained meter-to-desk/owner table for meters that have no deal history
outputs: a daily exception digest for each deal owner (e.g. Daren Farmer for HPL deals), listing meter, dates, volume, suggested deal to extend and action buttons
a shared open-exceptions list for volume management, with age, status and owner, replacing individual chase emails
an escalation notice to the desk lead for items older than the threshold or with a payment due date
a month-end summary: meter-days with flow but no deal, and volume parked on Strangers Gas
components: exception classifier (no deal / outside term / strangers gas)
owner-routing table (meter and deal to trader or desk)
per-owner daily digest email with pre-filled extend/create/write-off requests
open-exceptions tracker with ageing and escalation rules
decision log capturing who approved a write-off or buy back and why

implementation_steps: With volume management, list the exception types they chase today (no deal, partial-term deal, expired deal, Strangers Gas) and agree how each is defined at the meter-day level.
Get read access to Sitara deal tickets (meter, term, trader) and to the daily allocation data behind Volume Management and the allocation exception screen.

Build the comparison job and run it in shadow mode for one month next to the current email process. Check that its exceptions match what analysts such as Jackie Young and Aimee Lannou actually raised.
Build the owner-routing table from deal history, and send meters with no history to a desk default. Have the HPL and East desk leads confirm it.
Turn on the daily digest for one desk (HPL, Daren Farmer) with pre-filled extend/create requests and a status the owner can update with a reply or a click.
Add ageing and escalation rules, including a flag for items tied to counterparty payment deadlines.
Add the Unify path check so that a deal extension without a path is still shown as open.
Extend to other desks, and retire ad-hoc chase emails for exceptions the job already covers.
stays_manual: Deciding whether to extend a deal, create a new one or treat the flow as unauthorized. This is a commercial pricing decision for the trader.
Approving write-offs to unaccounted-for gas, buy backs and old prior-period adjustments, which need judgment on whether the gas can be invoiced (as in the Adonis case).
Deciding whether very old periods can be processed at all, e.g. periods before the move to Unify.
Settling volume disputes with outside parties such as Enerfin or HL&P when their numbers differ from ours.
risks: The evidence does not show how allocation data is stored or exported, so the effort to join it to Sitara by meter could be higher than estimated. Confirm data access before committing.
Meter numbers appear in several formats (98-9676, 0986725, 6387). If they are not normalized the job will produce false exceptions. Build a meter key mapping and test it in shadow mode.
Prior-period re-allocations change volumes after the fact, so an item may reopen. Track by meter-day and show reopened items as such instead of creating duplicates.
If owner routing is wrong, exceptions bounce between desks just as they do now. Have desk leads review the routing table, and give unassigned items a default owner.
A large digest could be ignored. Group items per owner, rank by volume and age, and keep the daily list short.
The evidence comes from a single mailbox (farmer-d), so how often this happens on other desks is uncertain.
success_metric: Number of meter-days with allocated flow but no covering Sitara deal at month-end close, and the median days from first flow to deal extension or creation
